title: Layer- and Orbital-Selective Mott Physics Driving Dimensional Crossover in Nickelate Superlattices
authors: Minjae Kim, Byungmin Sohn, Sangjae Lee
abstract: The design of quantum materials to manipulate dimensionality and electronic correlations is a central focus in the exploration of emergent phenomena. We propose a new correlated quantum material platform for realizing a layer- and orbital-selective Mott transition (LOSMT) in a nickelate heterostructure by combining bilayer and monolayer LaNiO$_3$ separated by a monolayer LaAlO$_3$ spacer under compressive strain from the LaAlO$_3$ substrate. The LOSMT emerges from the layer-dependent dimensional confinement of the apical Ni($d$)-$z^2$ orbital and strain-induced lifting of the orbital degeneracy. The monolayer LaNiO$_3$ exhibits an orbital-selective Mott insulating phase with a Mott gap in the Ni($d$)-$z^2$ orbital, whereas the bilayer LaNiO$_3$ exhibits a multi-orbital metallic phase, triggering the orbital-selective Mott transition upon cooling $via$ inter-layer hybridization of the Ni($d$)-$z^2$ orbitals. Calculations within the density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) framework reveal that the LOSMT drives a dimensional crossover by enabling out-of-plane electronic transport through the metallization of the localized apical Ni($d$)-$z^2$ orbital, while the planar Ni($d$)-$x^2-y^2$ orbital remains itinerant across the transition. The emergence of the LOSMT provides a new pathway for engineering correlated quantum materials toward unconventional superconductivity and Mott-transistor functionalities.
summary: This work investigates a nickelate superlattice to realize a Layer- and Orbital-Selective Mott Transition (LOSMT) using DFT+DMFT calculations. The transition is shown to fundamentally change the electronic structure by activating out-of-plane conductivity via the z^2 orbital. This mechanism offers a novel pathway for engineering correlated quantum materials with tunable dimensionality.
main_problem: The study aims to design quantum materials capable of manipulating dimensionality and electronic correlations by realizing a layer- and orbital-selective Mott transition (LOSMT).
main_result: The LOSMT drives a dimensional crossover by activating out-of-plane electronic transport through the metallization of the localized apical Ni(d)-z^2 orbital, while the planar orbital remains itinerant.
method: The research employs advanced theoretical calculations using the Density Functional Theory plus Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT) framework.
model_or_system: The system is a nickelate superlattice, specifically a heterostructure of bilayer and monolayer LaNiO3 separated by LaAlO3 spacer, subjected to compressive strain.
key_observables: Temperature-dependent, orbitally-resolved density of states (DOS), orbital occupations, and Fermi surface evolution.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction (U=6.0 eV) and Hund's coupling (J=0.7 eV); the transition temperature (T_LOSMT) is key.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the e_g-only projector method and relies on fitting self-energies on the Matsubara axis.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure and temperature-dependent DOS, Fermi surfaces changing from 2D to quasi-2D across T_LOSMT, and self-energies confirming selective correlation effects.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the goal (LOSMT). It then uses DFT+DMFT calculations to track orbital occupations and DOS across temperature, demonstrating the transition mechanism and its consequence on electronic dimensionality.
why_interesting: The concept of using a Mott transition as a tunable knob to control dimensionality is highly relevant to understanding correlated quantum materials and emergent electronic states.

Figure 5. Schematic illustration of the LOSMT and di- mensional crossover in LNO1–LAO1–LNO2–LAO1. (a) For T > TLOSMT, the Mott insulating z2 orbital in LNO1, with lower and upper Hubbard bands (LHB and UHB), blocks in- terlayer electron transfer between the two LNO2 layers. (b) For T < TLOSMT, a coherent quasiparticle peak (QP) devel- ops at the Fermi level in the z2 orbital of LNO1, enabling interlayer electron transfer between the two LNO2 layers.
